segments: fzf (fuzzy finder) is a general-purpose command-line fuzzy search tool. Its operating model is simple: read a list from stdin → filter interactively → write the selected result to stdout.
Compared with Ctrl+R (history search), fzf is general-purpose: it can search file lists, process lists, git branches, or any list of text.
Jump to the beginning / end of the line
After installing fzf, enable shell integration to replace the default Ctrl+R and Ctrl+T:
Ctrl+R — fuzzy-search command history (replaces the native binding)
Ctrl+T — fuzzy-search files in the current directory and paste the path
Alt+C — fuzzy-search directories and cd to one
Select a file and preview its contents

The assignment, read -d, and process-substitution examples above use Bash. -r, -o, and -p are the GNU xargs options used here. Terminating processes and running cherry-pick change state, so first inspect the selected PID or commit and the working tree. fzf is only a selector; you still need to check the upstream list and downstream operation. Ordinary newline-delimited lists are unsuitable for filenames containing newlines. fzf --bash/--zsh/--fish requires a version that supports that interface; for older versions, enable integration using the scripts supplied by the installed package.
